claim: Verkada: "Camera license about $249/camera/year on a 1-year term (~$220/yr at 3-10 year terms); camera MSRP from $799 (reseller price page)"
problem: The cited page (hts.pro/solutions/verkada-pricing) contains no dollar figures at all - it is a 'request a quote' page that only says each device has hardware plus a 1/3/5/10-year license. I also opened verkada.com/pricing, which lists $799 MSRP for the CD22 indoor dome but shows no $249 camera license and no per-year license figure. The $249 and ~$220 numbers are unverified, and the '$799 reseller price page' citation is wrong (the $799 is a manufacturer MSRP on verkada.com).
fix: Either cite https://www.verkada.com/pricing/ for the $799 CD22 MSRP and delete the $249/$220 license figures, or cite a page that actually states the license price. If no reliable public license price exists, write 'license price not published; resellers quote per device'.

problem: The cited Rhombus pricing page shows license '$149' per camera and references 'Professional or Enterprise license' types, but states no $199 figure and does not say the license is annual. The 'per year' and '$199 Enterprise' details are not on the page.
fix: Rewrite as 'license $149/camera (Professional tier; term not stated on the public page)' and drop or source the $199 Enterprise figure.

claim: Pilot benchmarks: "Rhombus ~$748 per camera-year for a cloud camera"
problem: On the Rhombus pricing page, $748 is R200 hardware ($599) plus ONE 1-year license ($149) - a first-year total, not a recurring per-camera-year cost. Presenting it as an annual rate overstates the recurring benchmark by roughly the hardware price.
fix: State 'R200 camera + first-year license = $748 MSRP; license renews at $149/camera (term per page)'.

claim: Hardware: "Reolink 4K PoE cameras (CX810 / RLC-811A) ... $129.99-$139.99 each" citing store.reolink.com/poe-ip-cameras/
problem: The cited URL returns HTTP 404 (also /us/poe-ip-cameras/ 404), so the price could not be confirmed at all. Worse, the brief's own Frigate source (docs.frigate.video/frigate/hardware/) explicitly says many users report issues with 4K-plus Reolink cameras and to 'stick with 5MP and lower for Reolink', and recommends Dahua/Hikvision - so the recommended camera contradicts the cited technical source.
fix: Re-cite a live Reolink product/price page (verify the actual price before quoting it), and add the Frigate caveat or switch the recommendation to a 5MP model.

claim: Measured outcome: "A 2025 evaluation of a major ALPR expansion found vehicle stops and recoveries increased but little evidence the expansion reduced violent crime generally"
problem: The paper's abstract (Shjarback & Sarkos, Justice Evaluation Journal 8(2), 2025, DOI 10.1080/24751979.2025.2473363) says the Atlantic City ALPR expansion 'did not reduce violent crime, but was associated with reductions in shootings, motor vehicle thefts, and property crime', and that use 'may be more siloed in certain investigative units rather than for patrol functions'. It says nothing about vehicle stops or recoveries increasing - that is the older Arizona study's finding. Reporting only the null violent-crime result also drops the study's positive findings, which cuts the other way.
fix: Restate as: '2025 ITS evaluation of Atlantic City's ALPR expansion found no reduction in violent crime overall but associations with reductions in shootings, motor vehicle theft and property crime (single city, quasi-experimental).'

claim: "2016 (NIJ-funded randomized experiment, Arizona)" for the LPR patrol experiment
problem: The NIJ publication page for 'Combating Vehicle Theft in Arizona' shows no 2016 date; the NIJ report was published December 2011 and the journal article in Criminal Justice Review in March 2012. The 2016 year appears to be wrong.
fix: Change to 2011 (NIJ report) / 2012 (journal article) and re-cite.

claim: "A separate employer-biometric bill (A1494) was introduced but not enacted in the 2024-25 session."
problem: A1494 (2024-25) concerned businesses' use of facial recognition / remote biometric recognition involving consumers at physical locations, not employer biometric monitoring of employees. The 'not enacted in 2024-25' part appears correct, but the description mislabels the bill, and the cited source (P.L. 2023, c.266) does not mention A1494 at all.
fix: Reword to 'a bill regulating commercial use of facial recognition at physical locations (A1494, 2024-25) was introduced but not enacted' and cite the bill text, not the NJDPA.

claim: Pilot cost: "Pilot total roughly $6,000-$12,000 installed: hardware $1,800-$3,500, installation 40-70 hours at $75-$125/hr ($3,000-$8,750), plus $0-$500"
problem: The stated line items sum to $4,800 on the low end and $12,750 on the high end, so the components exceed the quoted $12,000 ceiling (and the low end is below $6,000).
fix: Reconcile: e.g. '$5,000-$12,750' or tighten the labor band (40-60 hrs) so the sum matches the headline range.

claim: Mercy Housing: "about $43,000 installed cost, $23,000 grant, first-year savings estimated at $11,606 with a 32% initial water-use reduction"
problem: The Better Buildings page and its /printpdf variant both failed to load for me, so the $43,000 and $23,000 figures could not be confirmed. Independent search results corroborate only the 32% initial reduction and the $11,606 first-year estimate (and the note that savings decayed). The brief does disclose the page did not load, but the dollar figures remain unverified.
fix: Label the $43,000/$23,000 explicitly as 'unverified - taken from search index, page unopenable' or replace with the corroborated figures and a source that loads.

claim: Hardware: "Raspberry Pi AI HAT+ 13 TOPS (Hailo-8L) ... $70 list" citing raspberrypi.com/documentation/accessories/ai-hat-plus.html
problem: That documentation URL returns HTTP 403, so the price is not confirmable at the cited URL. The $70 price is correct, but it comes from Raspberry Pi's product/news pages, not the cited doc.
fix: Re-cite https://www.raspberrypi.com/products/ai-hat/ (or the launch post) which states $70 for the 13 TOPS version.

claim: Legal: "No New Jersey statute specifically regulates landlord cameras in common areas (searches of the NJ statutes and secondary summaries found none)", marked confirmed: true
problem: This is an absence-of-law claim, not a rule that can be 'confirmed' from a source. The cited URL is N.J.S.A. 2C:14-9, which does not and cannot establish that no other statute applies. Marking it confirmed overstates certainty.
fix: Set confirmed to false (or 'negative finding, low confidence') and keep the 2C:14-9 citation only for the privacy-limit sentence.

claim: Legal: "False accusation risk from automated detection or plate reads" entry, with source_url https://doi.org/10.1111/1745-9133.12419
problem: The entry is correctly labelled as an inference, but the attached URL is the CCTV-effectiveness meta-analysis, which says nothing about defamation, fair housing or misidentification liability. Attaching an unrelated source to an unsourced inference invites the reader to think it is supported.
fix: Remove the source_url (leave it blank as 'no source - inference') or replace with a source that actually discusses misidentification/defamation exposure.
